newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservatives ready for any poll date-chairman.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservatives ready for any poll date-chairman.

text.p: The chairman of Britain's ruling Conservative Party refused on Wednesday to be drawn into frenzied media speculation about the timing of an election.
"Whenever the Prime Minister announces a date, we will be ready," Brian Mawhinney told a news conference at the party's London headquarters.
He had been asked whether data showing a 67,800 fall in the number of jobless in January provided a good launch-pad for an election in March.
British newspapers said on Wednesday that Prime Minister John Major would have to make up his mind this week if he wants to call a snap election on March 20.
This would enable Major to avoid a parliamentary by-election going ahead on February 27 in the north-west constituency of Wirral South.
Two opinion polls have suggested that the Conservatives are set for a morale-sapping defeat by the opposition Labour Party in the seat, which they won easily at the 1992 general election.
Major himself has suggested his favoured date for a 1997 general election in May 1. The latest possible date is May 22.
